title: Review of c20's depression neural-field comets: SIMD replicates on fresh seeds 11 and 12; many fissions are break-ups of isolated elongated comets
summary: Re-ran the claimed world unchanged on seeds 11 and 12 (128^2, T=600). Both start from correlated noise over the whole domain and settle by t~24 into a gas of 26-75 comets with an active head and adaptation wake; comets move 19-27 body lengths and elongated comets break into comets (42 and 33 persistent splits, generation 9 and 5, merge/split 0.36 and 0.29). A fission detector of my own (fission_isolation.py) found 199 and 228 one-frame break-ups; the parent's median gap to the nearest other body over the three frames before was 5-6 px (about 0.6 body diameters, within the inhibitory kernel range), with 12-19 events at >= 8 px, and the most isolated ones (isolated_fission_s11/s12.png) show a single comet stretching into a bar and pinching into two comets with nothing nearby. Supported for S, I, M, D at L6[L2].

verdicts.track_note: I did not re-trace the claim's track 433 (seed 0); in my seed 11 the lineage 88>121>220>304>366>409>489>497>518 is a chain of persistent splits whose last daughter 518 travels 15.0 body lengths, and 123 (born of 79 at frame 10) travels 26.9, so the comets that divide are the comets that swim

controls_run.D: fission_isolation.py on rerun seeds 11 and 12: parent gap to nearest body median 5.1 / 5.7 px; 12 / 19 events with gap >= 8 px

verdicts.limitation: Individuals are activity pulses (L2), not material bodies; labkit finds 0-2 persistent tracks at K=20 because collisions churn identities, so lifetimes are judged from tracks.png. Most fissions happen with a neighbour within the kernel's inhibitory range (median gap ~0.6 diameters), so the population-level birth rate is partly collision-driven, although isolated break-ups do occur. My runs were T=600, not 1000.
